title: By the winds sent out, one gust after another.
subtitle: Why the surah swears by the wind
then: Ibn Masud reported this surah was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ {idea}in a cave at Mina{/idea}, and he learned it fresh from his mouth. Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas and others said the "ones sent forth" are {idea}the winds{/idea}; some said angels. Umm al-Fadl said it was {reward}the last thing she heard him recite, in the Maghrib prayer.{/reward}
now: A breeze through the window on a hot night. You barely notice it. {idea}The word used here is "sent."{/idea} Every gust is dispatched, like a message, by the One who also promised the Day.
old: The wind is just air moving around.
new: Even the wind is sent. Nothing in the world is purposeless.
try: Next time you feel a breeze, say SubhanAllah and remember it was sent.

title: And by the winds that blow with violent force.
subtitle: The same air, now a storm
then: Ibn Jarir affirmed that these {trap}are the winds{/trap}; Arabs said winds 'asafat {trap}when they roar with their blowing.{/trap} {idea}The One who sends a breeze can send a storm.{/idea}
now: A storm warning on your phone. Trees bending, power out, you sitting in the dark with candles. {idea}You feel how small you are.{/idea} The same power will bring the Day.
old: Storms are just bad luck.
new: The power behind a storm is the power behind the Day.
try: During the next strong wind, make a short dua for safety and mercy.

title: And by the winds that spread the clouds.
subtitle: Winds that carry mercy
then: Ibn Kathir says these are {idea}winds that scatter clouds across the sky{/idea} by Allah's will; Abu Salih said it is the rain. He cites the verse: {reward}He sends the winds as glad tidings before His mercy.{/reward}
now: Clouds gather after a dry month. Farmers watch the sky, you watch the forecast. {reward}The wind that brings them is part of a system built for you.{/reward}
old: Rain just happens when it happens.
new: The winds carry rain by design. Mercy is sent before it arrives.
try: When it next rains, make a dua. Rain is a time of mercy.

title: And by the angels who separate truth from falsehood.
subtitle: The ones who bring the dividing line
then: Ibn Kathir says here there is {idea}no difference of opinion: these are the angels.{/idea} They descend with Allah's command to the messengers, {idea}separating truth from falsehood, guidance from misguidance, lawful from forbidden.{/idea}
now: Everything online is blurred: opinions, hot takes, "it depends." You lose the sense of what is actually right. {idea}The revelation is the line that does not blur.{/idea}
old: Right and wrong are mostly up to each person.
new: Allah sent a clear line through His angels. I can find it.
try: When you are unsure about something today, check what the Quran says first.

title: And by the angels who deliver the reminder.
subtitle: Revelation reaching the messengers
then: Ibn Kathir says the angels {idea}bring the revelation to the messengers.{/idea} It is called dhikr, a reminder. {reward}It was carried with care, all the way down to you.{/reward}
now: You get dozens of reminders a day: meetings, bills, birthdays. You tap them away. {idea}This one was delivered by angels.{/idea} It deserves more than a swipe.
old: The Quran is one more thing on my list.
new: The Quran is a reminder Allah sent through angels, meant for me.
try: Set one phone reminder today that is only for reading a few verses.

title: To excuse some, and to warn others.
subtitle: Two purposes of the message
then: Ibn Kathir says the revelation contains {reward}exemption or absolvement for the creatures{/reward} and {trap}a warning of Allah's torment if they oppose His command.{/trap} {idea}It opens a door and marks a cliff edge.{/idea}
now: A doctor tells you your blood sugar is high. It sounds like bad news. But it is also the moment you can still fix it. {reward}A warning in time is a gift.{/reward}
old: Religious warnings are just there to scare me.
new: A warning comes with an excuse attached: a way to be cleared.
try: Read one warning verse today and ask: what way out does it offer me?

title: What you are promised will surely happen.
subtitle: The point of all five oaths
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}this is the subject of the oaths.{/idea} The Hour, the horn, the raising of bodies, the gathering of first and last, {reward}and every doer repaid for his deed: good for good, evil for evil.{/reward} {idea}It will come to pass.{/idea}
now: You make promises you mean to keep: I will call, I will pay you back, I will be there. Some slip. {idea}This promise does not slip.{/idea}
old: The Day might happen. Who knows?
new: It will happen. Winds and angels are sworn by to make that clear.
try: Do one good deed today with the promise of repayment in mind.

title: When the stars are wiped out.
subtitle: The lights that guided travelers go dark
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}their light will leave{/trap}, comparing it to the verses about stars falling and scattering. In Makkah, people {idea}navigated deserts by these stars.{/idea}
now: You go camping and see the night sky without city lights. Thousands of stars, ancient and steady. {idea}Even they will go out.{/idea} The promise of the Day is steadier than they are.
old: The stars will be there long after me.
new: The stars have an end. What Allah promised does not.
try: Look up at the night sky tonight for one minute and remember this verse.

title: When the sky is split open.
subtitle: The roof over the world cracks
then: Ibn Kathir says it is {trap}cleft asunder, its sides fall and its edges become weak.{/trap} The sky that looked like the most solid thing {idea}opens like a cracked shell.{/idea}
now: You look up on a blue afternoon and the sky feels like a ceiling that will always hold. {idea}This verse says it will crack.{/idea} What are you building under it?
old: The sky is the most permanent thing there is.
new: Even the sky will open. Only what I do for Allah stays.
try: Do one thing today that will still matter when the sky splits.

title: When the mountains are blown away like dust.
subtitle: No trace of them left
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}they will be removed and no sight or trace of them will remain.{/trap} He cites the verse where {idea}the earth becomes a level plain and all people are gathered, none left behind.{/idea}
now: You drive past the mountains on a family trip. They were there when your grandparents were young. {idea}They will be gone.{/idea} So will every big problem that feels like a mountain to you today.
old: My problems are like mountains: huge and fixed.
new: Even mountains will be dust. My problems are smaller than they look.
try: Name one worry that feels like a mountain, and hand it to Allah in dua.

title: When the messengers are gathered at their appointed time.
subtitle: The witnesses called forward
then: Ibn Abbas said it means {idea}gathered{/idea}; Mujahid said {idea}postponed{/idea}; Ibrahim said {idea}promised.{/idea} Ibn Kathir links it to the verse where {reward}the Prophets and witnesses are brought forward and judgment is given with truth.{/reward}
now: You read about the prophets as stories for children. Nuh, Musa, Isa, Muhammad ﷺ. {idea}They will be present that Day, as witnesses to whether the message was heard.{/idea}
old: The prophets are figures from the past.
new: The messengers will be gathered to testify. Their message is for me now.
try: Send salawat on the Prophet ﷺ ten times today.

title: For which Day was all this delayed?
subtitle: A question to make you lean in
then: Ibn Kathir says: {idea}for which Day are the messengers postponed and their matter awaited, until the Hour is established?{/idea} He cites: {reward}do not think Allah will fail to keep His promise to His messengers.{/reward}
now: A trial date keeps being moved. The other side starts acting like it will never happen. {idea}Delay is not cancellation.{/idea}
old: If it has not happened yet, it probably will not.
new: It is delayed to a set Day. The delay is time given to me.
try: Use one delayed thing today, a free hour, as time to prepare.

title: For the Day of Sorting.
subtitle: The Day everyone is separated
then: The answer to the question: {idea}the Day of Sorting Out{/idea}, the Day when the people of Paradise are separated from the people of the Fire. Ibn Kathir calls it {idea}the Day when it is judged between them with truth.{/idea}
now: At work, at school, in the mall, everyone is mixed: honest and dishonest, kind and cruel, all in the same queue. {idea}One Day the queues split.{/idea}
old: In the end, everyone ends up in the same place.
new: There is a Day of sorting, and I am choosing my line now.
try: Do one thing today that belongs in the line you want to stand in.

title: And what will make you know what that Day is?
subtitle: Too big to imagine
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah asks this {idea}to magnify its matter.{/idea} The listeners in Makkah had demanded the Day as a joke. {trap}The question tells them they have no idea what they are asking for.{/trap}
now: You hear about the Day of Judgement so often it sounds normal, like a weather report. {idea}This verse stops you: you do not actually know what it is.{/idea}
old: I have heard enough about the Day already.
new: Whatever I think the Day is, it is bigger.
try: Sit for one quiet minute today and just think about standing before Allah.

title: Woe, that Day, to those who denied it was coming.
subtitle: The first refrain: after the Day of Sorting
then: This is the first of ten times this line comes. Here it follows {idea}the Day of Sorting and the undoing of the sky{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says it means {trap}woe to them from Allah's torment that is coming.{/trap} The surah introduction says Makkah's people had demanded the Day as a joke.
now: Someone mocks the idea of judgement on a podcast and the room laughs. You laugh along so you do not look strange. {idea}This verse asks where you will stand when the joke is over.{/idea}
old: Joking about the Day is harmless.
new: Denying the Day, even laughing it off, is something I do not want to be part of.
try: Next time the Day is mocked around you, do not laugh along.

title: Did We not destroy the earlier peoples?
subtitle: History as evidence
then: Ibn Kathir says these are {trap}those who rejected the messengers and opposed what they brought.{/trap} The surah moves from the Day itself to {idea}evidence the listeners could already see: ruins of nations before them.{/idea}
now: You read about empires that seemed unbeatable and then vanished. It feels like a history lesson. {idea}The verse asks you to read it as a mirror for your own heart.{/idea}
old: What happened to past peoples has nothing to do with me.
new: Past peoples are a warning about the same choices I make.
try: Think of one habit of the arrogant you see in yourself, and drop it today.

title: And later ones will follow the same way.
subtitle: The pattern does not stop
then: Ibn Kathir says it means {trap}those who are similar to them.{/trap} The rule is not about a time or place. {idea}It is about behavior.{/idea}
now: You think the warnings in the Quran were about people back then. Arrogance, ingratitude, mocking the truth. {idea}The same behavior gets the same outcome, in any century.{/idea}
old: Those warnings were for people long ago.
new: The warning follows the behavior, not the date. I check my own.
try: Ask yourself today: which of those old behaviors do I still carry?

title: This is how We deal with the criminals.
subtitle: One rule for all
then: The verse states the rule plainly. Ibn Jarir explained these verses as {idea}the earlier ones destroyed, the later ones made to follow, because Allah deals with criminals this way.{/idea} {trap}No one gets a pass for being rich or strong.{/trap}
now: You see people with money or connections dodge consequences. It seems like rules are for the poor. {idea}This verse says Allah's rule has no VIP list.{/idea}
old: Powerful people always get away with it.
new: No one escapes Allah's rule. It is the same for everyone, me too.
try: Fix one small unfair thing you got away with, even if no one noticed.

title: Woe, that Day, to the deniers who ignored history.
subtitle: Second refrain: after the fallen nations
then: The refrain returns right after {idea}the fall of earlier peoples and the rule that later ones like them follow.{/idea} Ibn Jarir read the warning together with "thus We deal with the criminals." {trap}To see ruins and keep denying is the woe here.{/trap}
now: You watch a documentary about a fallen civilization, then go straight back to the same pride and carelessness they had. {idea}The lesson was in front of you.{/idea}
old: History is interesting, but not a warning for me.
new: Seeing the end of others and changing nothing is its own kind of denial.
try: After the next history video you watch, write one lesson for yourself.

title: Did We not create you from a lowly fluid?
subtitle: Your beginning as proof

row.title: how can you think I am unable?

then: Ibn Kathir says this is {idea}weak and lowly compared to the power of the Creator.{/idea} He cites the hadith where Allah says: {trap}Son of Adam, how can you think I am unable, when I created you from something like this?{/trap}
now: You stand in front of the mirror after the gym, proud of yourself. {idea}Remember where you came from.{/idea} Not to feel small, but to see how able your Maker is.
old: I am too complex to be brought back.
new: I came from almost nothing. Bringing me back is not hard for Him.
try: Next time pride rises today, remember your beginning and say Alhamdulillah.

title: Then We placed it in a safe, secure lodging.
subtitle: The womb, built for protection
then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}the womb has been prepared for this, as a protector of what is placed in it.{/reward} {idea}Before you could do anything, you were already being looked after.{/idea}
now: You worry about keeping your kids safe: car seats, vaccines, locks on the cupboard. {reward}Allah kept you safe before your mother even knew you were there.{/reward}
old: I have always had to look after myself.
new: Allah was protecting me before I could do anything at all.
try: Call your mother, or make dua for her, today.

title: For a known, set time.
subtitle: Even your birth was on schedule
then: Ibn Kathir says this means {idea}a fixed period of time, from six months to nine months.{/idea} The same Lord who {reward}set the day of your birth{/reward} has set the Day of your return.
now: Expecting parents count the weeks on an app. A due date is circled on the calendar. {idea}Your birth had a known time. So does your death, and so does the Day.{/idea}
old: Life's timings are just chance.
new: My beginning had a set time. My end and the Day do too.
try: Use a few minutes of today as if your time were known and short.

title: We measured it out, and how excellent a Measurer.
subtitle: Every detail decided by Him
then: After the drop, the womb, and the fixed term, Allah says {reward}We measured, and We are the best to measure.{/reward} Ibn Kathir notes these verses remind people of {idea}His favor{/idea} and use the first creation as proof of the second.
now: Your height, your voice, the day you were born, the family you were born into. {reward}None of it was a mistake.{/reward} The One who measured all of that is excellent at it.
old: Parts of how I was made feel like mistakes.
new: Allah measured me with care, and He is the best at measuring.
try: Thank Allah for one thing about yourself you usually complain about.

title: Woe, that Day, to the deniers who forgot their own beginning.
subtitle: Third refrain: after the creation in the womb
then: This time the refrain follows {idea}the creation of man from a drop, kept safe, for a known term.{/idea} The evidence is not in history books now; {trap}it is in their own bodies, and they still deny.{/trap}
now: You hold a newborn at the hospital. Tiny fingers, perfect ears, all from nothing. Then you go home and forget about it. {idea}The proof was in your arms.{/idea}
old: I need more evidence to really believe in the Day.
new: The evidence is my own body. Ignoring it is the real problem.
try: Look at your own hand today and say: the One who made this will raise me.

title: Have We not made the earth a container?
subtitle: The earth that holds everything
then: Ibn Abbas said kifat means {reward}a place of shelter.{/reward} Mujahid said {idea}it holds the dead so nothing of them is seen.{/idea} The earth was made to hold people, in life and after.
now: You walk on concrete all day and never think about the ground. {reward}It holds your house, your food, your city.{/reward} One day it will hold you.
old: The ground under me is nothing special.
new: The earth is a shelter Allah made to hold me, now and later.
try: Go barefoot on grass or soil for a moment today and remember this verse.

title: For the living on top, for the dead within.
subtitle: One earth, two kinds of residents
then: Ash-Sha'bi said: {idea}its interior is for your dead and its surface is for your living.{/idea} Mujahid and Qatadah said the same. {reward}The earth holds both, and gives both back on the Day.{/reward}
now: You walk through a graveyard on the way to the shop. The living on the path, the dead beneath. {idea}You are just on the top layer for now.{/idea}
old: The graveyard is a different world from mine.
new: The same earth holds me and the dead. I will move from its top to its inside.
try: Visit a graveyard this week, or make dua for the dead when you pass one.

title: Firm mountains, and sweet water to drink.
subtitle: Stability and refreshment, given
then: Ibn Kathir says the mountains hold the earth {reward}so it does not shake and sway.{/reward} The water is {reward}cold and delicious, from the clouds or from the springs He makes gush forth.{/reward}
now: You fill a glass from the tap without a thought. Somewhere it fell as rain, ran through mountains, and came to you. {idea}The verse says: We gave you that drink.{/idea}
old: Water is just a utility I pay for.
new: Every sip of fresh water is Allah giving me to drink.
try: Drink your next glass of water slowly and say Alhamdulillah after.

title: Woe, that Day, to those who drank His water and denied Him.
subtitle: Fourth refrain: after the earth, mountains, and water
then: Ibn Kathir explains this one directly: {trap}woe to whoever reflects on these created things that show the greatness of their Creator, and after that keeps rejecting Him.{/trap} The ground, the mountains, the water were {idea}gifts in their hands.{/idea}
now: You live on Allah's earth, drink His water, breathe His air, and go whole days without a word of thanks. {idea}The woe is for seeing the gifts and still turning away.{/idea}
old: I can enjoy the world without thinking about who gave it.
new: Using His gifts while ignoring Him is the denial this verse warns about.
try: Thank Allah out loud for three ordinary things before you sleep tonight.

title: Go now to the very thing you called a lie.
subtitle: The denied becomes the destination
then: Ibn Kathir says this is said to {trap}those who denied the final abode, the reward, Paradise and the Fire.{/trap} {idea}The very thing they called a lie is where they are sent.{/idea}
now: You say "that will never happen to me" about a debt, a diagnosis, a broken relationship, and keep doing what leads there. {idea}Denying a road does not stop it from arriving where it goes.{/idea}
old: If I refuse to believe it, it cannot touch me.
new: Denial does not stop the destination. It only makes the arrival a shock.
try: Face one thing today you have been telling yourself is not real.

title: Go to a shadow of smoke in three columns.
subtitle: A shade that is not shade
then: Ibn Kathir says it is {trap}a flame of fire rising with smoke, so strong it splits into three columns.{/trap} The righteous later in the surah are {reward}among real shades and springs.{/reward}
now: You chase something that looks like rest: the binge, the escape, the late-night habit. It looks like shade. {idea}It turns out to be smoke.{/idea}
old: Anything that looks like relief must be relief.
new: Some shade is smoke. I want the real shade Allah promises.
try: Swap one false escape today for a real rest: sleep early, or two rakahs.

title: No cool shade, and no help against the flame.
subtitle: The shadow that protects from nothing
then: Ibn Kathir says this shade of smoke {trap}will not have a shade, nor will it benefit against the flame.{/trap} {idea}It will not protect them from the heat at all.{/idea}
now: You hide behind things: your title, your family name, "everyone does it." They feel like cover. {idea}On that Day they give no cover at all.{/idea}
old: My position and excuses will protect me.
new: Nothing I hide behind gives real shade. Only good deeds do.
try: Drop one excuse you hide behind and do the thing instead.

title: It throws out sparks as large as forts.
subtitle: The scale of what was denied
then: Ibn Masud said {trap}like forts.{/trap} Ibn Abbas and others said {trap}like tree trunks{/trap}; Ibn Abbas described timber of three cubits they called qasr. {idea}The point is scale: even the sparks are enormous.{/idea}
now: You flick a match and blow it out. Fire seems small and controllable. {idea}This verse tells you the sparks alone are bigger than buildings.{/idea} Better to stay far away.
old: I can handle whatever comes.
new: Some things are too big to handle. I want to stay far from them.
try: Ask Allah tonight to protect you and your family from the Fire.

title: As if the sparks were dark camels.
subtitle: An image the listeners knew
then: Mujahid, Al-Hasan and Qatadah said these are {trap}black camels{/trap}; Ibn Abbas said {trap}ropes of ships bundled together.{/trap} {idea}The listeners in Makkah knew camels and ropes well.{/idea} The picture was made to be felt.
now: Warnings that are vague slide off you. A clear picture sticks. {idea}The Quran gives a picture so you take it seriously, not to scare you for fun.{/idea}
old: Warnings about the Fire are just exaggeration.
new: The images are clear so I take them seriously and turn toward safety.
try: Ask Allah three times today, in your own words, to keep you safe from the Fire.

title: Woe, that Day, to those who mocked what they now see.
subtitle: Fifth refrain: after the smoke and sparks
then: This refrain comes after the scene of {trap}the smoke in three columns and sparks like forts.{/trap} Earlier refrains came after signs in the world. {idea}This one comes after the place itself, the thing they called a lie in verse 29.{/idea}
now: You scroll past a reminder about the Hereafter: just another post. {idea}This verse is the moment the post becomes real.{/idea} The time to take it seriously is while it is still a post.
old: Reminders about the Fire are just words on a screen.
new: Words now, sight later. I would rather listen now.
try: Read one reminder you would usually skip, all the way through.

title: This is a Day they will not speak.
subtitle: The talkers fall silent

row.title: always mine
sub: I can talk my way out

then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}they will not be able to speak.{/trap} The proof is established and {trap}they cannot say anything.{/trap} He notes the Day has stages, and {idea}this is one of them.{/idea}
now: You are the one who always has a comeback: in meetings, in arguments, in the comments. {idea}One Day the clever reply will not come.{/idea} Use your words now for things you want said.
old: I can always talk my way out of anything.
new: There is a Day words fail. I should use mine well now.
try: Use your words today for one apology or one sincere thank you.

title: Not even allowed to offer an excuse.
subtitle: The time for excuses has passed
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}they will not be granted permission to speak so they can make excuses.{/trap} {idea}The proof will be established against them.{/idea} The door for explaining yourself is in this life.
now: You plan to explain yourself later: to Allah, to your parents, to yourself. Later keeps moving. {idea}The window for "I am sorry" is open today, not forever.{/idea}
old: I will explain myself when the time comes.
new: The time to explain myself to Allah is now, in repentance.
try: Turn one excuse into a sincere istighfar today.

title: Woe, that Day, to the deniers left with no words.
subtitle: Sixth refrain: after silence and no excuse
then: Ibn Kathir says that after all the details of this stage, {trap}He says: woe that Day to the deniers.{/trap} This refrain follows {idea}the loss of speech and excuse.{/idea} Those who had plenty to say against the truth now have nothing.
now: Think of all the words you have spent this week: complaints, gossip, arguments you did not need. {idea}Words are a currency that runs out.{/idea}
old: Words are cheap. I can always say more.
new: My words now are my only chance to speak for myself. I spend them carefully.
try: Spend one conversation today saying only what is true and kind.

title: The Day of Decision: you and all who came before, gathered.
subtitle: Every generation on one plain
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}will gather all of them by His power on one plain, make them hear the caller, and make them see.{/idea} The earlier peoples from verse 16 {trap}are there, and so are the listeners.{/trap}
now: Your great-great-grandparents, whose names you do not know. The people in your history books. You. {idea}All on one plain, at once.{/idea}
old: Judgement feels like something for other people.
new: Every generation stands together, and I will be among them.
try: Make dua today for your ancestors, even the ones you never knew.

title: If you have a plan, try it against Me.
subtitle: The end of every scheme
then: Ibn Kathir calls this {trap}a serious threat and a harsh warning{/trap}: if you can save yourselves from My ruling, do it. {idea}But you cannot.{/idea} He cites the hadith: {idea}My servants, you cannot reach My harm to harm Me.{/idea}
now: You plan, angle, and arrange to get out of things: the deadline, the bill, the hard conversation. {idea}There is one meeting no scheme gets you out of.{/idea}
old: With a clever enough plan, I can get out of anything.
new: No plan works against Allah. The only plan that works is turning to Him.
try: Drop one scheme you are running to avoid something, and face it honestly.

title: Woe, that Day, to the deniers whose plans ran out.
subtitle: Seventh refrain: after the challenge to plot

row.title: Allah's mercy
sub: what they could have relied on

then: This refrain follows {trap}"if you have a plan, use it against Me."{/trap} The people of Makkah had {idea}mocked the message and resisted it.{/idea} Now, gathered with all of history, {trap}they have no plan left.{/trap}
now: You trust your own cleverness more than you trust Allah: the backup plan, the clever workaround. {idea}Cleverness has an end. His mercy does not.{/idea}
old: My smartness is my best protection.
new: My best protection is not my cleverness but Allah's mercy.
try: Before your next big decision today, pray two rakahs or make a short dua first.

title: The mindful will be among real shades and springs.
subtitle: The opposite of the smoke

row.title: the mindful
sub: did the duties, left the forbidden

then: Ibn Kathir says the people of taqwa are those who {idea}worship Him by doing the obligations and leaving the forbidden.{/idea} They will be {reward}in gardens and springs, the opposite of the wretched under black smoke.{/reward}
now: A hot afternoon, and you find a tree with deep shade and a water fountain next to it. Pure relief. {reward}That is the picture, made eternal.{/reward} It is built from ordinary daily choices.
old: Taqwa sounds like something only for very religious people.
new: Taqwa is doing what is asked and leaving what is forbidden, one day at a time.
try: Leave one small forbidden thing today, quietly, for Allah.

title: And whatever fruit they desire.
subtitle: Their wish is answered
then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}from every kind of fruit, they will have whatever they request.{/reward} The ones who held back their desires for Allah {idea}now have their desires met.{/idea}
now: You walk past the bakery while fasting. You skip the second helping so you can give some away. {reward}Every desire you set aside for Allah is waiting for you, answered.{/reward}
old: Holding back my desires means losing them.
new: What I hold back for Allah, He gives back in full.
try: Pick one craving today and give it up for Allah's sake.

title: Eat and drink happily, for what you used to do.
subtitle: Spoken to them with kindness
then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}this will be said to them out of kindness.{/reward} The deniers were told "go to what you denied." {idea}The mindful are told "eat and drink, for what you used to do."{/idea}
now: You come home after a long shift and someone has dinner ready, and says: sit, you earned this. {reward}Imagine Allah saying that to you.{/reward}
old: My small good deeds will be forgotten.
new: Allah will welcome me with kindness for what I used to do.
try: Do one good deed today you would love to hear mentioned that Day.

title: This is how We reward those who do good.
subtitle: A rule, not a one-off
then: Ibn Kathir says this restates the point: {reward}this is Our reward for whoever does good.{/reward} Earlier the surah said {trap}thus do We deal with the criminals.{/trap} {idea}Both are rules. Both are fair.{/idea}
now: You wonder if your effort at being good is noticed: patience with your kids, honesty at work, the extra mile for a neighbor. {reward}This is the rule: it is rewarded, every time.{/reward}
old: Being good does not really pay off.
new: Allah has a rule: those who do good are rewarded like this.
try: Do something today with excellence, not just enough.

title: Woe, that Day, to the deniers who missed all this.
subtitle: Eighth refrain: after the reward of the good
then: This refrain comes right after {reward}the reward of the good: shade, springs, fruit, a kind welcome.{/reward} {idea}Here the woe is about what the deniers gave up.{/idea} Ibn Kathir notes the mindful are in the opposite state of the wretched.
now: A friend offers you a seat on a trip of a lifetime and you say no because you could not be bothered. Later you see the photos. {idea}This woe is for missing what was offered.{/idea}
old: Denying the Day only costs me if the Fire is real.
new: Denial also costs me the Garden that was offered to me.
try: Think of the Garden for one minute today, and say: O Allah, I want it.

title: Eat and enjoy a little. You are criminals.
subtitle: A short enjoyment, then the end
then: Ibn Kathir says this is addressed to the deniers as {trap}a command of threat{/trap}: enjoy yourselves {trap}for a short, small, brief time.{/trap} He compares it to "We let them enjoy a little, then drive them to a severe punishment."
now: Friday night, takeaway, a new show, no thought of tomorrow. Nothing wrong with the food. {idea}The question is whether "a little while" is all you are living for.{/idea}
old: Life is for enjoying now. Worry about later, later.
new: Enjoyment here is short. I want it to lead somewhere lasting.
try: Before your next meal, say Bismillah and thank Allah after.

title: Woe, that Day, to the deniers who chose the little.
subtitle: Ninth refrain: after the short enjoyment
then: This refrain follows {trap}"eat and enjoy a little, you are criminals."{/trap} Ibn Kathir says after the little while {trap}they will be driven to the Fire already mentioned.{/trap} {idea}The woe is for trading forever for a little.{/idea}
now: You spend your best years on things that will not matter in a decade: the grudges, the status games, the endless scroll. {idea}A little, for a lot.{/idea}
old: A little fun now is worth the risk.
new: Trading forever for a little is the worst deal there is.
try: Give ten minutes today that you would have spent scrolling to something for the Hereafter.

title: When told to bow, they do not bow.
subtitle: Pride that will not bend
then: Ibn Kathir says when they {idea}were ordered to pray with the believers{/idea}, {trap}they refused and turned away arrogantly.{/trap} Of all their actions, the surah names this one at the end: {idea}not bowing.{/idea}
now: The adhan goes off on your phone during a meeting. You swipe it away. Not because you are against prayer, just because bowing right now feels awkward. {idea}Notice what is really stopping you.{/idea}
old: Missing a prayer is just about being busy.
new: Sometimes what stops me bowing is a little pride. Bowing breaks it.
try: Pray your next prayer on time, even if it is a little awkward where you are.

title: Woe, that Day, to the deniers who would not bow.
subtitle: Tenth refrain: after refusing to pray

row.title: a head that will not bow

then: This is the last of the ten refrains. It comes after {trap}"when told to bow, they do not bow."{/trap} Ibn Kathir says they {trap}refused arrogantly.{/trap} {idea}Denial is not only a belief. It shows up as a refusal to bow.{/idea}
now: You believe in the Day. You would never deny it. But when the time for prayer comes, your body says no. {idea}The verse asks what your actions are saying.{/idea}
old: As long as I believe, not praying is a small thing.
new: A head that will not bow is a kind of denial too. I want mine to bow.
try: Make one sujud today a little longer and ask Allah for steadiness.

title: After this, what words will they ever believe?
subtitle: If not the Quran, then what?
then: Ibn Kathir says: {trap}if they do not believe in this Quran, what talk will they believe in?{/trap} He links it to the verse asking what speech after Allah and His signs they will believe. {idea}The surah has given everything; there is nothing after it.{/idea}
now: You keep waiting for the perfect lecture, the perfect video, the moment that will finally change you. {idea}The words are already here, in your hands.{/idea}
old: I will change when I hear something powerful enough.
new: Nothing will be more powerful than the Quran. It is already here.
try: Read this whole surah once this week, slowly, start to finish.
